findings.title: The rule 'stock execute never sends signals' does not say what happens to leftover runner tmux windows on the MERGED held/partial reclose path
findings.detail: The round-2 HIGH is fixed: §5.2 now does a census-only check under the lock, adds a processHandling=refuse primitive, persists a stock-cleanup context, and has race tests. lsof census was checked read-only on this host (exit 0). One gap remains. The reclose finalizer's physical pass runs closeRunner/window cleanup before worktree settlement. A tmux kill-window sends SIGHUP to the pane's processes, which can include a founder-driven shell in a leftover runner pane (founders watch and drive panes in cmux). The plan forbids stopping the body and path-reap, but says nothing about window teardown. So a leftover pane can either be killed before the census runs, silently weakening the no-signal promise, or make every such item fail as process_present. State which: stock mode must not kill windows (such items are excluded as process_present/window_present), or it may kill only panes whose processes are all 2919-registered pure viewers of a proven-dead body. Add a negative test.

findings.title: The absorbed FLY-2754 never-started branch needs an 'is it alive' census that 2919 cannot attribute without a binding
findings.detail: §12 routes 2754 provenance checks into the 2919 provider's trusted never-started branch. It forbids carrying over the helper-level pgrep/ps/window scans, yet still requires the provider to prove 'no socket/spawn lock/owner/restart/live body'. 2919's observeExecutionProcesses returns unknown whenever there is no binding (origin/flywheel-FLY-2919 execution-process-liveness.ts:119). Its OS census attributes processes only through a binding or nonce. Never-started executions have neither. The branch will therefore either always be unknown, in which case §12 recovers nothing, or someone will reintroduce the FLYWHEEL_EXEC_ID env scan inside the provider. Spell out exactly which facts count as 'no live body' for a bindingless never-started execution (for example, a typed proof that the runtime was never invoked plus closed launch claim plus zero owner/spawn_inflight plus no socket/lock), and which component owns any execution-id census.

findings.title: Reusing lifecycle_apply_claims for stock directory receipts needs an explicit scope/key and CAS
findings.detail: putApplyClaim (StateStore.ts:32131) is an unconditional upsert keyed only on (root_uuid, approved_hash) and has no effect-scope column. closeoutIssueWithSnapshotGuard replays any `complete` report stored under the same key. The plan requires a scope separate from the whole-issue closeout epoch and a requestId+digest unique mapping. Say concretely whether that means a new column or a namespaced key, and use a compare-and-set status transition rather than a blind upsert, so a stock directory receipt can never collide with or overwrite a founder apply epoch.
